newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal will be in EMU from start - minister.
newsitem.headline: Portugal will be in EMU from start - minister.

text.p: Portugal's Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco said on Thursday his country will be among European Union members launching the single currency in 1999.
"We are going to be in the euro (the single currency). We are going to be in the first wave," he said during a parliamentary debate on the economic and monetary union (EMU).

In a rare show of unity, the Socialist government and its main opponents tabled a joint motion on Thursday backing the bid to be in the first group of countries to wed their economies in the single currency.
The move was triggered by doubts expressed by some northern European countries about whether Italy, Spain and Portugal, the so-called 'Club Med' countries, should join EMU from the start.

Sousa Franco said that access to the first wave of monetary union had to be decided according to rules laid down in the Maastricht Treaty, the EMU blueprint, and could not depend on the whim of member states.
"It has got to conform to the rules," he said.

Sousa Franco said that the tight budgetary and anti-inflation policies being followed by the government in order to comply with the EMU entry criteria were policies that would be needed even if the single currency did not exist.
The government's 1997 budget plan calls for a deficit of 2.9 percent of gross domestic product (GDP), just below the three percent EMU ceiling. The deficit was around four percent in 1996.
